title: Software search benchmark
question: How many array probes do linear and binary search use for four fixed queries on 16 sorted values?

benchmark.workload: Fixed successful and unsuccessful queries on one 16-element array. No timing or representative-workload claim.
benchmark.fairness: Both algorithms receive the same array and queries; correctness uses the standard-library bisect reference; sorting costs are excluded.

answers.purpose: Rehearse an explicit calculation before adapting a protocol to real research. These inputs are constructed teaching data, not collected observations.
answers.sample: Fixed teaching fixture, not a sample-size recommendation or a representative population.
answers.safeguards: Synthetic public inputs under the repository license; no participants, clinical validation or research approval implied.
answers.validation: Recompute using the command in Analyze and compare with the frozen output. Inspect invalid-input tests and the domain-specific limits.
answers.review: Self-check through code and known-answer tests; no independent research review.
answers.units: An array of even integers 0–30; queries 0, 14, 30 and 31.
answers.comparison: How many array probes do linear and binary search use for four fixed queries on 16 sorted values?
answers.outcome: Array probes per query, including the unsuccessful query.
answers.procedure: Verify sorted unique inputs; run both search algorithms; compare found values with bisect_left; retain per-query probe counts.
answers.analysis: Check correctness first; summarize paired performance over workloads and repeats. Distinguish counted operations from elapsed time; retain outliers and failures.
answers.limitations: A probe inspects one array element, not one CPU operation. Deterministic synthetic workload; no elapsed-time or general-performance claim. Sorting costs are excluded.
answers.interpretation: The computed quantities describe this fixture only; they do not establish a finding about patients, deployed systems or the physical world.
answers.disclosure: Teaching material assembled with automated assistance and checked through executable calculations where supplied. No independent review is claimed.
